analysis.investment_thesis: Puravankara fails both Magic Formula screens decisively — Earnings Yield of ~3.2% (EBIT ₹291 Cr / EV ~₹8,976 Cr) is far below the 6% minimum, and ROCE of 6% is less than one-third the 20% threshold for a good business. With finance costs (₹555 Cr) nearly double EBIT (₹291 Cr), the underlying business cannot service its own debt — this is a capital-consuming enterprise, not a capital-compounding one.
key_strengths: High promoter holding (75%) signals alignment and conviction in the business
Gross margin of 44% indicates pricing power at the project level
Revenue recovering — ₹2,185 Cr in FY24 from a trough of ₹955 Cr in FY22
key_risks: Finance cost (₹555 Cr) exceeds EBIT (₹291 Cr) — interest coverage ratio of 0.52x, deeply insolvent at the earnings level
Debt has surged to ₹4,497 Cr (2025) from ₹2,627 Cr (2022) while equity has shrunk from ₹2,042 Cr to ₹1,619 Cr
Operating cash flow flipped to -₹531 Cr in FY25 after a strong ₹896 Cr in FY24 — highly volatile, project-lumpy
red_flags: Net loss of ₹183 Cr in FY25 — Magic Formula requires positive EBIT to function; earnings yield is near-meaningless here
ROIC/ROCE of 6% is catastrophically below the 20% threshold — this business destroys capital at scale
Real estate developer: Greenblatt explicitly excludes capital-structure-distorted industries like this
Finance costs growing at 9.6% CAGR over 9 years while EBITDA grew only 0.6% — debt is compounding faster than earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EV = Market Cap (₹5,340 Cr) + Net Debt (₹4,332 Cr - ₹696 Cr cash) = ~₹8,976 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income 2025) = ₹291 Cr. Earnings Yield = 291/8,976 = 3.2% — needs to be above 12% to be attractive. ROCE at 6% is similarly disqualifying; the business earns barely above nothing on its capital base. Both legs of the Magic Formula are broken simultaneously. The company also earns a negative net profit (-₹183 Cr in FY25), meaning the formula cannot even be properly applied.

The structural problem is existential: annual finance costs of ₹555 Cr are nearly 2x EBIT. Every rupee earned from operations is consumed and then some by interest alone, forcing continued debt accumulation (borrowings up 70% in three years to ₹4,497 Cr). Equity has eroded from ₹2,042 Cr in FY22 to ₹1,619 Cr in FY25 — the company is slowly consuming its net worth. Real estate developers like Puravankara are explicitly the type of capital-intensive, balance-sheet-heavy businesses the Magic Formula is designed to avoid. At a 23x forward P/E and EV/EBITDA of 21x, the market is pricing in a recovery the fundamentals do not yet support.
